newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close firmer despite political woes.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close firmer despite political woes.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed firmer on Wednesday as investors bought up several blue chips despite a minor campaign clash in Jakarta, brokers said.
"Because some blue chips were already at bargain levels, investor bought back the stocks. This is the right time anyway," a broker with a Hong Kong-based firm said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed 1.27 points higher, or 0.19 percent, at 654.09 points after touching an intra-day low of 652.15 points. Advancers beat decliners 57 to 55, with 70 counters unchanged. Total turn-over was estimated at 317 billion rupiah, compared with 319 billion rupiah on Tuesday.

"Volume-wise, today's trading is relatively good," another broker said. He added the slow trade in Jakarta was also linked to a holiday in Singapore and in Malaysia on Wednesday combined with Thursday's local holiday.
Brokers expected trading to remain slow on Friday as many investors preferred to wait and see what would happen as the campaign for the May 29 general elections came to a close.

Analysts said the U.S Federal Reserve decision on Tuesday to keep interest rates steady did not have much impact on market sentiment in Jakarta as investor were more concerned about domestic political news.

Indonesia's violence-marred campaign for May 29 general elections resumed on a quieter note on Wednesday, with only one report of an isolated clash between students and supporters of the ruling Golkar party.
Witnesses said some 2,000 students of the IAIN Islamic University on the southern outskirts of Jakarta threw stones at Golkar supporters after an altercation just outside the campus.
Blue chip Telkom, cigarette makers Sampoerna and Gudang Garam and cement producers Semen Gresik and Semen Cibinong were among the targets of bargain hunters, brokers said.
Small property firm Mas Murni Indonesia was the most active stock after the exhange resumed trading in the counter in the afternoon session.
Trading on the stock was suspended for the morning session due to its sharp rise on Tuesday, bourse officials said.
Mas closed 25 rupiah higher at 850 rupiah on a volume of 36.7 million shares on what brokers said was speculative interest.
"Personally, it's fundamentals are not really good. It was mostly due to revived talk of a possible take-over by a foreign company or a rights issue," a broker with a major local firm said.
